(a) Classify basketry materials into natural and synthetic, giving three examples of each. [6 marks]
(b) Distinguish between pliable and rigid materials, giving one example and one use of each. [6 marks]
(c) State three qualities of a good basketry material. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Natural (any three): raffia, cane/rattan, bamboo, palm fronds/leaves, grasses, sisal, straw, bark fibres
3 marks: Synthetic (any three): plastic strips, nylon cord, polythene, synthetic raffia, wire, paper cord
3 marks: Pliable: flexible, bends easily without breaking; e.g. raffia, grasses, thin cane - used as weavers/for coiling and plaiting
3 marks: Rigid: stiff, holds shape; e.g. thick cane, bamboo, wood - used as stakes, frames and handles
3 marks: Any three (1 each): strong/durable; flexible when prepared; available and affordable; even in thickness; resistant to pests and mould; takes dye/finish well
questions.explanation: Natural: raffia, cane, bamboo, grasses; synthetic: plastic strips, nylon, wire. Pliable materials bend (raffia for weavers); rigid ones hold shape (thick cane for stakes and frames). Good materials are strong, flexible, available and durable.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe how cane is prepared for weaving a basket. [6 marks]
(b) State three chemical or non-chemical methods of preserving stored basketry materials. [3 marks]
(c) Explain three ways of preserving the natural sources of basketry materials. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: Any three steps described (2 each): sort and grade cane by thickness; cut to required lengths; soak in (warm) water until pliable; wrap in damp cloth to mellow; split/shave where needed; bleach or dye if required
3 marks: Any three (1 each): sun-drying before storage; storing in dry ventilated place; treating with insecticide/fungicide; using naphthalene or neem leaves; smoking
6 marks: Any three explained (2 each): avoid bush burning; replant/re-afforestation; harvest selectively without uprooting; protect wetlands where raffia grows; community laws on harvesting
questions.explanation: Cane is graded, cut, soaked until pliable, mellowed, then split or dyed as needed. Store dry and treat against pests. Preserve sources by stopping bush burning, replanting and selective harvesting.

questions.stem:
(a) Name five basketry tools and state the use of each. [10 marks]
(b) State five ways of caring for basketry tools and observing safety in the workshop. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: Any five tools with correct use (2 each): bodkin - opening spaces/inserting stakes; rapping iron - beating down weaving; side cutters - cutting stakes/cane close to work; knife - cutting and splitting; round-nose pliers - bending/squeezing cane; measuring tape/rule - measuring; shears/scissors - cutting raffia; screw block - holding stakes in square work
5 marks: Any five (1 each): clean and dry tools after use; oil metal tools to prevent rust; sharpen cutting tools; store in a box/rack; carry pointed tools with points down; cut away from the body; keep floor free of cane off-cuts
questions.explanation: Bodkin opens the weave, rapping iron packs it, side cutters trim, knife cuts and splits, pliers bend cane. Care: clean, oil, sharpen and store tools; cut away from the body and keep the floor clear.

questions.stem: Describe the following basketry techniques: (a) randing; (b) pairing; (c) waling; (d) coiling; (e) plaiting. [15 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Randing: a single weaver passes in front of one stake and behind the next, row after row
3 marks: Pairing: two weavers worked alternately, each passing in front of one stake and behind the next, crossing between stakes (a form of twining)
3 marks: Waling: three or more weavers worked in sequence, each passing in front of two or more stakes and behind one, giving a strong ridged band
3 marks: Coiling: a continuous bundle of fibre is wound in a spiral and stitched to the previous coil
3 marks: Plaiting: flat strands are interlaced diagonally or at right angles over and under each other without stakes, e.g. mats
questions.explanation: Randing uses one weaver in and out of stakes; pairing two twisted weavers; waling three or more for strength; coiling stitches a spiral bundle; plaiting interlaces flat strands without stakes.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between decoration and finishing in basketry. [4 marks]
(b) Describe three methods of decorating a basket. [6 marks]
(c) Describe two methods of finishing a basket. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Decoration: adding features that make the article beautiful/attractive
2 marks: Finishing: final processes that make the article neat, durable and ready for use
6 marks: Any three described (2 each): using coloured (dyed) weavers; weave variations (e.g. waling bands, open work); scorching; spraying with paint; attaching beads, cowries, shells, leather or fabric; embroidery
5 marks: Any two described (award up to 5): trimming loose ends; singeing loose fibres; binding/lashing edges and handles; making borders; varnishing/lacquering; sanding
questions.explanation: Decoration beautifies; finishing makes the article neat and durable. Decorate with dyed weavers, weave variations, scorching and beads. Finish by trimming, singeing, binding borders and varnishing.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between fixed cost and variable cost, giving two examples of each for a basketry business. [6 marks]
(b) A basket maker spends ₦18,000 on materials and ₦6,000 on other costs to make 12 shopping baskets. Calculate (i) the cost of one basket; (ii) the selling price of one basket if a profit of 25% on cost is required. [5 marks]
(c) State four factors that determine the price of a basketry product. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Fixed cost: does not change with the quantity produced; e.g. rent, equipment, salaries of permanent staff, licence fees (any two)
3 marks: Variable cost: changes with quantity produced; e.g. cane, raffia, dyes, varnish, transport per order (any two)
2 marks: Cost of one basket = (18,000 + 6,000)/12 = ₦2,000
3 marks: Selling price = 2,000 + 25% of 2,000 = ₦2,500
4 marks: Any four (1 each): cost of production; demand; competition/prices of similar goods; quality and design; customers' income; location/market; time and skill involved
questions.explanation: Fixed costs (rent, equipment) do not vary with output; variable costs (cane, raffia) do. Cost per basket = ₦24,000/12 = ₦2,000; selling price with 25% profit = ₦2,500. Price depends on cost, demand, competition, quality and market.
